sections.heading: The setup
sections.body: The S&P 500 closed Sep 29 at 7,671, roughly flat on the month (-0.2%) and mid-range between its 1-month low of 7,552 and high of 7,765. The Nasdaq 100 sits at 30,339, up 3.0% over the month and in the upper part of its 1-month range (28,938 to 30,732). Euro Stoxx 50 is 1.6% lower on the month at 6,320. VIX is 16.0, up from 14.9 at the start of the window but inside its 14.2 to 17.8 range. Seven index-universe names report Oct 5-9, with consumer-defensive the largest group (PEP, STZ, LW) plus single names in tech, industrials, financials and materials.

sections.heading: What to watch
sections.body: Tue Oct 6 is the busiest day: STZ and LW report into consumer-defensive (median -0.5% off recent prints across 379 names), FDS into financials (+0.4%) and RPM into materials (+0.1%). Wed Oct 7: APLD US reports into technology, median +1.5% across 623 names. Thu Oct 8: PEP US reports into the same consumer-defensive group. Fri Oct 9: DAL US reports into industrials, median -0.8% across 651 names. None of these sectors is among the top movers in the reaction table, so this week's reports sit in a quiet part of it.

sections.heading: Signals to trust
sections.body: Mining (+6.6% median, 178 tickers, 2,630 news items) leads the reaction table, followed by alternative-asset-management (+2.9%, 6 tickers, 241 news items) and copper (+2.6%, 6 tickers, 248 news items). Oil-gas is the main negative at -2.5% on 33 names with 1,021 news items. Mining and oil-gas have thick news windows; none of the seven names reporting this week belong to these sectors.
